name: Dull Blue
lede: Dull Blue is a muted, mid-toned slate blue named by the 2010 xkcd color survey, common enough to turn up in a Monet sunset and a Fra Angelico Madonna alike.

sections.title: A crowd name for a grayed blue
sections.body:
The only recorded source for Dull Blue is the xkcd survey of 2010, following the plain modifier grammar *dull* plus [[blue]] [1]. At hex #49759C it measures lightness 48 and chroma 26 in LCH, and the nearest ISCC-NBS block reads as a moderate blue, 4.8 units off [1].

Its closest named neighbor is [[flat-blue|Flat Blue]], 2.5 units away and more vivid, followed by [[stormy-blue|Stormy Blue]], 2.8 units off and almost the same color [2]. [[queen-blue|Queen Blue]] sits 3.9 units away, also almost the same [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This match appears in 0.58% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive (139 paintings, as photographed); the within-painting lens narrows that to 64 [3]. In our archive it is more common than 53% of the named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, present in 0.8% of the 1,674 paintings we have from that decade (13 paintings), 2.3 times the rate its museums would predict [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays an accent across its 64 appearances by lightness rank within the painting [3]. The earliest match dates to 1405, 605 years before the name's 2010 record, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin and a look-alike hue in an aged photograph is not proof of a pigment or dye [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so the match is a screen comparison, not a pigment identification [3].
